_source: Deterministic parse of raw Telair PBX CSV exports (ExportCallRecords, InboundCalls_Detailed, CallQueue_Detailed per queue) via scripts/parse_call_logs.py, chained against assets/data/reports/2026-10-14/call-logs.json. This date is unusually clean — summary, queue breakdown, patientServiceKpi, longestWaitPerQueue and inboundByStaff (all 11 names, calls AND durations) all match Daily Operations Report - 15th October 2026.pdf exactly. Only outboundByStaff's per-agent minutes (usual small rounding gaps) and the outboundTenDayTrend (a second consecutive date where the PDF's own chart diverges sharply from the chain-verified total — see _outboundTenDayTrendNote) carry notes this date.
_summaryVsGrandTotalNote: This file's own summary (296 total/266 accepted) matches the PDF's own pie chart exactly (296 total, 266 accepted/90%, 30 missed/10%). The queue-level grandTotal below sums to 265 accepted/30 missed (295 total) — 1 short of the pie, the same small pre-existing PDF-internal inconsistency (its own cover doesn't equal its own queue-breakdown sum) seen on prior dates, not introduced here.
_tenDayTrendNote: accepted/missed/answerRatePct/overallAvgWaitSec all chain-match 2026-10-14's own committed trend exactly at positions 0-8; position 9 matches the PDF's own printed charts exactly across the board (Call Answer Rate 90%, Overall Average Wait Time 50 sec, and the Call Volume chart's own 266/30 split).
_queuesNote: accepted/missed/avgWaitSec for all four queues chain-match 2026-10-14's own committed data exactly at positions 0-8, and all four queues' accepted/missed/avgWaitSec at position 9 match the PDF's own queue breakdown and per-queue 10-day charts exactly — including Canberra Vasectomy's unusual 3 accepted/3 missed split (a 50% miss rate on a very small sample), which the PDF's own chart confirms verbatim rather than a parsing glitch.
_patientServiceKpiNote: All five figures match the PDF's own Patient Service KPI panel exactly, including avgCallHandlingSec (152 sec, no rounding gap this date).
_staffCountNote: All 11 inboundByStaff names match the PDF's own printed Inbound Calls - All Staff table exactly on both calls and duration — clean match, no gap this date (calls sum to 266, matching the PDF's own pie chart exactly).
_outboundDurationNote: outboundByStaff's own call counts match the PDF's own 13-name outbound staff table exactly for every name (37/29/21/14/13/8/7/6/4/4/2/1/1, summing to the confirmed 147-call total, which also matches this file's own summary.totalOutbound and the PDF's own 'Total Outbound Calls = 147 Calls' header exactly). Several per-agent durationMins values differ from the PDF's own printed minutes by 1-6 (e.g. De Ang Renfree 46 here vs 52 printed, Andrew Davies 54 vs 57, Hannah Searle 36 vs 39), while Jessica Hinchy/Kiara Pfeffer/Lyneham - Rec 1 match exactly — consistent with each source rounding individual call durations to the nearest minute before summing in a slightly different way, not a data error; recorded verbatim rather than adjusted to match.

_outboundTenDayTrendNote: Chain-matches 2026-10-14's own committed trend exactly at positions 0-8 (this field covers ALL outbound extensions — reception + other — not just the reception-staff subset in outboundByStaff; 147 reception + 101 other = 248). FLAG FOR USER REVIEW (second consecutive date): the PDF's own 'Outbound 10 Day Trend Reporting' chart this date prints [173,186,305,320,268,200,235,172,105,160] for the same 10 labels — matching our chain-verified totals exactly at positions 0-6, then diverging at position 7 (Wed 14-Oct: PDF still shows 172 vs our chain-verified 252, the same gap flagged yesterday, unchanged), position 8 (Thu 15-Oct in this chart's own forward count... actually Wed14Oct here; PDF 105 vs chain 177) and position 9 (Thu 15-Oct, today: PDF 160 vs our chain-verified 248, an 88-call gap). This now looks like a systemic, persistent divergence in how the PDF's own chart renders its most recent ~3 days rather than a one-off glitch — everything else on this page (summary.totalOutbound=147, the full outboundByStaff table) still matches the PDF exactly, so the discrepancy is isolated to this one historical trend chart's own generation.
_duplicateSourceNote: No duplicate CallGUIDs or other raw-source anomalies observed in any of the four CSVs for this date.
